comparison: Both evaluate claims C82-C87 about chromosome alignment's role in membrane scission. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about speculation (C87). Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning whether this demonstrates cell-cycle dependence rather than mechanical forces, and are confused why hcp-3 RNAi prevents scission but doesn't cause paired nuclei.

Both evaluate claims C97, C99 about lamina's role in nuclear shape and membrane fluidity. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as reasonable inferences appropriately qualified as speculative. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting these interpretations of lamina function.

Both evaluate claims C4, C76-C77, C109 about reduced spindle elongation in lmn-1 8A. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as a novel finding demonstrating bidirectional coupling. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED and highlight it as interesting, noting in point 12 that the nuclear membrane's role in spindle length regulation had not been discussed and could be emphasized in conclusions.

Both evaluate the temporal characterization of NEBD events (C35-C50). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with detailed quantitative data, noting some mechanistic interpretations involve reasonable inferences. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY with multiple concerns: why focus on scission site vs breakdown near centrosomes (point 1), confusion about terminology (point 2), questions about marker choices (point 4), and why LMN-1 signal remains in bright focus.

Both evaluate claims C105-C108 about the dissociation between membrane scission failure and paired nuclei. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, noting mechanistic explanations are speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, stating in point 11 that 'the short speculation at the top of page 11 does not seem enough' to explain the complex relationship.

Both evaluate background claims C8-C27 (and C1-C2, C28-C32, C88-C93 for peer review) about C. elegans embryology and nuclear envelope biology. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED, not challenging these background claims and focusing questions on new findings instead.

Both evaluate claims C66-C70 about membrane scission frequency and spindle elongation correlation. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, noting the mechanistic link is correlative. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, identifying in point 10 a major inconsistency: 83% of gpr-1/2 RNAi embryos lack scission but only 5% show paired nuclei, requesting better explanation of this relationship.

Both evaluate claims C60-C65 about differential effects of gpr-1/2 and klp-7 manipulations on lamina stability. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by quantitative fluorescence data, highlighting C65 as particularly important. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED, accepting that pulling forces contribute to lamina disassembly, though they raise mechanistic questions in point 9.

Both evaluate claims C78-C81 about the epistasis experiment showing lamina depolymerization is required for membrane scission. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as compelling evidence from a critical control experiment. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, accepting the hierarchical relationship, though they question in point 9 whether mechanical forces or cell cycle control is primary.

Both evaluate claims C94-C96, C98, C100 about PLK-1's role in lamina depolymerization. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by epistasis data, noting the conclusion that LMN-1 is the only target is inferential. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning in point 13 the connection to cortical pulling forces and noting that 'by this point in the manuscript, it seems that pulling forces have a secondary effect on scission.'

Both evaluate main conclusions C3-C7, C101-C102 about bidirectional relationship and coordination model. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED, well-justified by collective evidence. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, asking in point 13 'which one is the primary factor? How are the others comparable to the primary factor?' indicating confusion about hierarchical relationships in the coordination model.

Both evaluate claim C33 about the motivating hypothesis drawing analogy to human cells. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as appropriate framing for a hypothesis subsequently tested. Peer reviewers also find it SUPPORTED, not challenging this speculative claim that serves as motivation for experimental work.

Both evaluate claims C53-C58 (OpenEval) and C54-C58, C60-C65 (peer review) about gpr-1/2 RNAi effects. OpenEval finds C53-C58 SUPPORTED by quantitative dose-dependent data. Peer reviewers also find the overlapping claims SUPPORTED, accepting that gpr-1/2 RNAi enhances paired nuclei and that pulling forces contribute, though raising mechanistic questions.

Both evaluate claims about spindle elongation and membrane scission timing. OpenEval evaluates C71-C74 finding them SUPPORTED with strong correlation evidence, though C74's mechanistic interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C72-C74 (plus C3, C34, C51-C52, C69) as SUPPORTED, accepting this as a key contribution about pulling forces via spindle elongation.

Both evaluate prior work claims. OpenEval evaluates C1-C2, C6, C28-C32, C90 as SUPPORTED, summarizing Velez-Aguilera et al. 2020 findings. Peer reviewers evaluate broader background (C1-C2, C8-C32, C88-C93) as SUPPORTED without challenge, accepting established knowledge.

Both evaluate claims C96, C98 about INM protein localization after lmn-1 RNAi in plk-1ts embryos. OpenEval finds C96, C98 (among C88-C100) SUPPORTED by epistasis data. Peer reviewers find these claims UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging in point 8 that 'the distributions of both do appear very different' and that the claim is inconsistent with the images.

OpenEval evaluates C103-C108 about dissociation between scission and paired nuclei, finding them SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C103-C104 (plus C66-C68, C70) as UNCERTAIN, identifying in point 10 a major inconsistency between high scission failure rate and low paired nuclei rate.

OpenEval evaluates C91-C92 about FIB-SEM membrane fusion structures as SUPPORTED citations to prior work. Peer reviewers include these in broader background claims (R14) evaluated as SUPPORTED, not challenging these established findings from Rahman et al. 2020.

OpenEval evaluates C43 (among C35-C52) as SUPPORTED, noting it involves reasonable inference from morphological changes. Peer reviewers specifically challenge C43 as UNSUPPORTED in point 5, stating 'the authors do not provide any evidence that microtubules in fact are required for this shape' and calling it an assumption.

OpenEval evaluates C45 (among C35-C52) as SUPPORTED with reasonable inference about membrane deformations. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about C45 in point 3, questioning whether authors 'typically see protrusions, or a variety of deformations' and requesting more detail about what images show regarding pulling versus pushing.

OpenEval evaluates C3 (among C3-C7, C101-C102) as SUPPORTED main conclusion about pulling forces via spindle elongation. Peer reviewers evaluate C3 (among C3, C34, C51-C52, C69, C72-C74) as SUPPORTED, accepting this as a key contribution with requests for mechanistic clarification but no challenge to core finding.

OpenEval evaluates C69 (among C66-C70) as SUPPORTED evidence for mechanistic link between spindle elongation and scission, though correlative. Peer reviewers include C69 in claims evaluated as SUPPORTED (R1), accepting the correlation as supporting the role of pulling forces.

OpenEval evaluates C6 (among C1-C2, C6, C28-C32, C90) as SUPPORTED prior work about paired nuclei phenotype. Peer reviewers evaluate C6 (among C6, C94-C96, C98, C100) as UNCERTAIN, questioning the connection between plk-1ts experiments and cortical pulling forces and asking which is the primary factor.

OpenEval evaluates C4 (among C3-C7, C101-C102) as SUPPORTED main conclusion about lmn-1 8A reducing elongation. Peer reviewers evaluate C4 (among C4, C75-C77, C109) as SUPPORTED, highlighting this as interesting and novel for spindle length regulation.

OpenEval evaluates C5 (among C3-C7, C101-C102) as SUPPORTED main conclusion about pulling forces requiring depolymerized lamina. Peer reviewers evaluate C5 (among C5, C78-C81) as SUPPORTED, accepting the hierarchical relationship though questioning whether mechanical forces or cell cycle control is primary.
